links.outcome: Change in diagnostic accuracy and advice when varying patient age, sex, and race/ethnicity in prompts
links.effect: Diagnostic accuracy not significantly different across demographic groups; urgent care recommendations and demographic tailoring appeared significantly more for 75-year-olds vs 25-year-olds (P<.01), not across race/ethnicity or sex.
links.quote: ChatGPT's urgent care recommendations and demographic tailoring were presented significantly more to 75-year-olds versus 25-year-olds (P < .01) but were not statistically different among race/ethnicity and sex groups.

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy across demographic subgroups (age, race/ethnicity, sex)
links.effect: Diagnostic accuracy was not significantly different across demographic groups; ChatGPT matched WebMD in 91% of diagnoses, with 24% top diagnosis match.
links.quote: Diagnostic accuracy was not significantly different across demographic groups, including age, race/ethnicity, and sex.

links.outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT text (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) across demographics
links.effect: GPT text suitable for college students with no significant demographic variability; reading level is above typical patient health literacy targets.
links.quote: The GPT text was suitable for college students, with no significant demographic variability.

screen.reason: Evaluates ChatGPT's diagnostic accuracy and demographic bias using simulated patient symptom vignettes across age, sex, and race/ethnicity variations without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
